title: About the security content of iOS 27 and iPadOS 27
reliability_notes: Official Apple page. Credits Calif.io researchers for four CVE entries: CVE-2026-65409, CVE-2026-65410, CVE-2026-28968 and CVE-2026-86886 (the last was missed in the first extraction). An entry-update note dated October 19, 2026 follows CVE-2026-28968. Re-fetched on 2026-11-12: no entry for iOS 27.0.1, and no occurrence of the identifier CVE-2026-112611 or the handle pwnlambda. Re-read 2026-11-12. The page marks many entries as added or updated on 2026-10-19 and 2026-10-26 (C-071); CVE-2026-112608 is marked added on 2026-10-26 (C-070).
notes: publication_date is the iOS 27 release date from search metadata; the page itself carries later update dates.

title: Apple security releases
reliability_notes: Official Apple index. Shows 'This update has no published CVE entries' for iOS 27.0.1 and iPadOS 27.0.1, a 26 Oct 2026 row for iOS 27.2, a 09 Nov 2026 row for iOS 27.2.1, and an iOS 27.1 row for iPhone Duo dated 23 Oct 2026 with no CVE entries. The text extract truncates some month names; dates were read from the surrounding rows.
notes: Build numbers are not shown on this index.

title: Memory Integrity Enforcement
reliability_notes: Apple's own technical description. States MIE is built into all iPhone 17 and iPhone Air models, names the A19 and A19 Pro chips, and says the Secure Page Table Monitor protects the kernel allocator backing store and tag storage. It does not name the A17 Pro.
notes: Launch was September 2025; the exact day was not extracted from the page.

title: Apple Platform Security: Secure Page Table Monitor and Trusted Execution Monitor
reliability_notes: Apple's platform security guide, continuously updated. States SPTM is supported on A15-or-later and M2-or-later SoCs and replaces the Page Protection Layer on supported platforms. Re-read on 2026-11-12 for the memory-protection review. The OS-integrity section (page date January 28, 2026) states SPTM support on A15-or-later and M2-or-later SoCs, with SPTM and TXM replacing the PPL there. It states MIE availability on A19 and M5 processors or later. The support table's cells are images in the fetched copy, so per-chip cell values could not be read.
notes: The guide has no publication date.

title: iPhone 15 Pro - Technical Specifications

title: Dopamine releases
reliability_notes: GitHub API release records for opa334/Dopamine (30 most recent releases, 2.2.2 to 3.0.13), retrieved 2026-11-12, with release bodies read. Dopamine 3.0 (2026-08-07) lists a Titan PPL/SPTM bypass for iOS 16.5.1 to 17.3.1, a momentarius PPL bypass for A12 and A13, and states real-device SPTM support ends at 17.3.1 (C-065 to C-068). Releases 3.0.2 to 3.0.13 do not mention iOS 27 support (C-055). The official README on the default branch is stale (S-008).

notes: Stale documentation; cited to show the official matrix was not found here.

notes: The article credits a third-party researcher with posting stage video; that person is not named in this repository.

title: About the security content of iOS 27.2 and iPadOS 27.2
reliability_notes: Official Apple advisory for iOS 27.2 and iPadOS 27.2 (release date 2026-10-26 per Apple's release index). Entries give component, impact, description and credits. The extracted text contains 162 distinct CVE identifiers. Affected version ranges are not stated. Credits are recorded by organisation or handle only. The Apple release index gives 26 Oct 2026. The ipsw release date is 2026-10-26 18:33 UTC. The upstream reference gives 2026-10-27, which is probably a time-zone difference (C-046 scope).

title: Modern iOS Security Features: A Deep Dive into SPTM, TXM, and Exclaves (arXiv:2510.09272)
reliability_notes: Independent academic analysis of SPTM, TXM and Exclaves. The full HTML text (v1) was searched. Its firmware analysis uses iOS 18.4 (22E240) firmware for iPhone 16 (A18). It does not analyse the A17 Pro or iOS 27 firmware. Submitted 2025-10-10, before the iOS 27 release. Full-text search on 2026-11-12: the paper mentions A15 only in its SPTM and TXM availability statement. It does not mention A16 to A20, iOS 26, iOS 27, iPhone 15 or iPhone 17.

title: Works on iPhone 18 Pro: AI helps create untethered jailbreak for iOS 27.0.1
reliability_notes: Reputable German technology publication (English edition). States that the Calif.io team presented an untethered iOS 27 jailbreak at Hexacon, that the vulnerabilities used are not yet clear, and that the team's X profile had no further details. Its headline states that AI helped create the jailbreak. Secondary to the event. States that the team 'has developed the first reboot-proof jailbreak since iOS 9' (C-075).

title: Dank KI: Rebootfester Jailbreak für iOS 27.0.1 bis zum iPhone 18 Pro, untethered
reliability_notes: German edition of the heise report, dated 16.10.2026. States that the vulnerabilities used are not yet known. Describes the AI-assisted comparison of iOS 27.2 beta with 27.0.1 as theoretically possible ('theoretisch'), and says that another exploit for the August screen-sharing flaw apparently did not come from Calif.io. Does not quote the 'any iPhone' statement attributed to a team member (C-052).

title: iOS-27-Jailbreak: Sicherheitsforscher greifen auf KI-Support zurück
reliability_notes: German technology news, dated 18.10.2026. States that AI was used to find the exploit chain. Presents an AI-assisted comparison of the iOS 27.2 beta with iOS 27.0.1 as established. The team has not stated this method, and the heise articles call it theoretical (C-076). Not a primary source.
